disposition_reason: Cadmium by GF AAS in six fresh shiitake samples grown in São Paulo state (2006-2007) and eight imported dehydrated shiitake products from Japan and China (2009); per-sample dry-weight and in natura values in Table 3.

study.design: Retail and producer sampling, per-sample analysis
study.origin: Fresh: cultivated in Mogi das Cruzes, Suzano, Mirandópolis, Juquitiba and São Paulo cities; dehydrated: imported from Japan (3) and China (5)
study.market: Fresh bought from retail stores and directly from producers in São Paulo state; dehydrated bought from retail stores
study.method: HNO3/H2O2 block digestion, GF AAS (Zeeman, AAnalyst 800)
study.qa: NIST SRM 1577b bovine liver, INCT MPH-2 herbs and IAEA mushroom material, z-scores within 2; IAEA proficiency test

controls.control: Origin: shiitake grown in São Paulo state versus imported dehydrated from Japan and China
controls.outcome: Cd 0.102-0.207 mg/kg dw (São Paulo) vs 0.212-1.25 mg/kg dw (imported); ANOVA significant across São Paulo, Japan, China (F = 10.63); Japan vs China not significant

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum level for cadmium in cultivated mushrooms (as cited, Regulation EC 2006)

unresolved: The abstract gives the imported in natura range as 0.125 to 0.212 mg/kg, but Table 3 prints 0.0212 to 0.125 mg/kg; Table 3 used.
For fresh samples the printed in natura values (e.g. 0.118 dw to 0.0079) imply more than 90% water, while the text cites about 90%.
Sample codes may encode product names; they are replaced with numbered category labels.
